verifications.claim: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Launch date NET April 1, 2026'; R4: 'When No Earlier Than April 1'; R5: 'targeting ... Wednesday, April 1'; R7: 'NASA has set April 1 as the target launch date'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state NASA targeting April 1, 2026, as the launch date.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R2: 'planned 10-day Artemis 2 mission'; R3: 'Mission duration10 days (planned)'; R4: 'The 10-day flight'; R6: 'The 10-day mission'; R7: '10-day test flight'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly describe Artemis II as a 10-day crewed mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'orbit the Moon', 'around the Moon'; R3: 'lunar flyby', 'fly around the Moon'; R4: 'venture around the Moon'; R6: 'flyby ... around the moon'; R7: 'around the far side of the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission as a lunar flyby or orbiting/flying around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human spaceflight to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'For the first time since 1972, NASA is sending humans back'; R2: 'closest approach to the Moon in more than 50 years'; R3: 'first crewed deep-space and lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R6: 'first time humans have traveled ... to the moon since ... 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm it as the first crewed mission to lunar vicinity since 1972 (Apollo 17).

verifications.claim: The rocket and spacecraft are scheduled to roll to the launch pad on March 19, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'would be rolled out the following day [March 19]'; R5: 'targeting 8 p.m. EDT on Thursday, March 19, to start rolling'; 'originally scheduled for March 19'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm March 19 as the scheduled/targeted rollout date, though it was later delayed to March 20.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission duration is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R3: '10 days (planned)'; R4: '10-day flight'; R6: '10-day mission'; R7: '10-day journey'; R2: '10-day Artemis 2 mission'
verifications.reasoning: Identical to claim 2; sources explicitly state approximately/around 10 days.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R3: 'first crewed mission of the Orion spacecraft'; R4: 'first crewed mission on NASA's path ... SLS rocket and Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Sources, including NASA-linked, confirm it as the first crewed SLS/Orion flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II goal is testing systems for deep space, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'verify modern human capabilities in deep space'; R3: 'test and demonstrate optical communications ... life support systems'; R4: 'help confirm systems and hardware needed for early human lunar exploration missions'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe goals as verifying/testing systems for deep space/human lunar missions.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission was previously delayed from earlier in 2026 due to technical issues, including heat shield repairs and cold weather testing, as reported by Spaceflight Now and Space.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2 (Spaceflight Now): 'cold weather ... delayed ... earliest possible launch date'; R3: delays due to 'liquid hydrogen leak', 'helium flow issue', heat shield 'concerns' but 'Rather than replacing the heat shield'; R5: various technical delays/repairs; R6: 'heat shield improvements' not repairs
verifications.reasoning: Delays from early 2026 confirmed (R2 cold weather, R3/R5 technical issues), but no evidence of 'heat shield repairs' (sources say no replacement/repairs, just trajectory change/improvements); 'cold weather testing' misstates delay of testing due to cold weather.
